title: Chondrodermatitis nodularis helicis & ear nodules
summary: A painful, tender nodule on the rim of the ear that stops people sleeping on that side. Relieve pressure first; know the ear-nodule differentials (BCC, SCC, keratoacanthoma, gouty tophus, AK).

glance.think: A small painful crusted nodule on the helix or antihelix, worse lying on that side, in an older adult.
glance.engine: Pressure on cartilage with poor blood supply leads to inflammation and cartilage damage.
glance.backbone: Pressure-relief pillow or ring for 4–6 weeks; consider a potent topical steroid; refer if failing or atypical.
glance.never_miss: SCC or BCC of the ear (biopsy if not settling), keratoacanthoma (rapid crater), tophaceous gout.

what: A benign, **painful**, inflamed nodule of the ear cartilage and overlying skin. It is commonest on the **helix in older men** and on the **antihelix in women**.

The pinna is a **high-risk site for skin cancer**: it is sun-exposed and thin-skinned, and spread to the parotid and cervical nodes happens early. BAD 2020 classifies **ear cSCC as high-risk by site**.
cause: **Pressure-induced ischaemia.** Ear cartilage has little subcutaneous padding and a poor blood supply. Sustained pressure (sleeping on one side, headsets, phones, hats), cold or sun damage causes perichondrial inflammation and focal cartilage necrosis that extrudes through the skin. **One-sided sleeping is typical, e.g. after a stroke, or with arthritis or CPAP masks.** In [Case 2](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) with a previous right-sided stroke, ask which side she lies on.
Chronic UV (helix, especially in men with short hair), immunosuppression, and for gout, urate deposition in cool tissue.

list: A firm, round, 4–10 mm nodule with a **central crust, scale or keratin plug**, sometimes ulcerated.
**Exquisitely tender**: it wakes the patient at night when they lie on it, and **light squeezing causes disproportionate pain** (the course bedside test). Usually on the side the patient sleeps on.

head: Diagnosis
Clues
Photo
rows: Very tender, central crust, the side slept on
Indurated, keratotic or ulcerated, growing over weeks to months, bleeds. Often painless or mildly tender. ± palpable pre-auricular/cervical node
Rapid growth over **weeks**, a dome with a **central keratin crater**, may involute
Pearly, rolled edge, telangiectasia, slowly growing; often posterior ear or sulcus
Rough, flat-to-slightly-raised scale; not nodular or tender
Firm, **chalky white-yellow** papules on the helix/antihelix, may discharge, ± a history of gout, diuretics (e.g. thiazides)
Small, white, painless, bilateral helical-rim papules
Keratin projection; the **base** may be SCC

list: Clinical: site + pain + central crust + sleeping history.
Dermoscopy: central white-yellow keratin/ulcer with a radiating whitish "starburst" and peripheral dotted or linear vessels. It is **non-specific** and **cannot reliably exclude SCC/BCC**.

**Biopsy when:** atypical features (rapid growth, bleeding, induration, a size >1 cm, a rolled pearly edge, no pain); no improvement after **6–8 weeks of strict offloading**; immunosuppression; or patient anxiety.

diagnosis: Pain pattern, growth tempo, and palpation of regional nodes. Biopsy anything unexplained. Serum urate (when not in an acute flare) if tophi are suspected.
differentials: See *Ear nodule differentials* (SCC, BCC, keratoacanthoma, AK, gouty tophi, also cutaneous horn, wart, elastotic nodules of the ear, weathering nodules, chilblain).
As above. Also chilblain (cold, bilateral, purple), relapsing polychondritis (the whole ear red, sparing the lobe), and discoid lupus.
management: **Step 1: pressure relief, for everyone (first-line; the course answer)**

list: A **pressure-relieving device**: a CNH prosthesis/"ear protector" made of foam with a hole for the ear (sold OTC and online), a pillow with a hole, or a travel pillow; sleep on the other side. Remove headphone and phone pressure.
Resolution or major improvement occurs in a large proportion of patients within weeks to months. Recurrence is common if offloading stops.
Analgesia as needed. Emollient/protective dressing over the crust.

head: Option
Notes
rows: Low-quality evidence. IP-prescribable (e.g. betamethasone valerate 0.1%) for a short trial **only once SCC/BCC has been reasonably excluded**

Off-label. Small studies show benefit via vasodilatation. Headache and hypotension. **Check PDE-5 inhibitor co-prescription** (contraindicated). Not routinely available as a dermatology product in the UK
Surgical excision of the abnormal cartilage ± skin

management: **Refer:** **NG12 1.7.4** says to consider a suspected cancer pathway referral if SCC is suspected (a growing, indurated, bleeding, non-tender or atypical ear nodule). Refer routinely if CNH is not settling after 6–8 weeks of offloading.

list: **Suspected SCC or keratoacanthoma:** NG12 1.7.4, consider a **suspected cancer pathway referral**. BAD guidance is to **treat KA as SCC** (excise) because they cannot be reliably distinguished clinically.
Suspected BCC: NG12 1.7.5, routine referral, unless the site or size makes delay important (1.7.6). The ear is a high-risk "H-zone" site.
Gouty tophi: a GP/IP gout pathway. **Urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, treat to target <360 µmol/L, or <300 if tophaceous)**, per NICE NG219 (gout, 2022). Review diuretics.
AK: cross-reference the [older skin pages](condition:itch-xerosis-older-adults) notes see *Worked cases* (field therapy).

red_flags: Rapidly growing, ulcerating or bleeding ear nodule, or an ear nodule with a nearby lymph node: **suspected SCC**, suspected-cancer referral (NICE NG12).
pearls: [Case 2](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) medicines: aspirin is relevant only if a biopsy or excision is done. **Do not stop aspirin for minor skin surgery** (BSDS 2023; see the [skin surgery](condition:skin-surgery-preop) notes). Losartan and simvastatin are not causative.
Explain the mechanism ("a pressure sore of the ear cartilage"). Adherence to offloading for at least a month is the key to success.
**Painless** ear nodule plus rapid growth means think SCC/KA. **Very painful at night** means think CNH. But both can coexist, which is why non-resolving CNH gets a biopsy.
Check transplant or immunosuppressant history (azathioprine, ciclosporin, tacrolimus): cSCC risk rises up to 65–100× in organ transplant recipients.
